title: CTRT Security with Full-Tweak-Space Counter Cycling
summary: Existing NSIV analysis limits CTRT’s IV space to the block-space size; it remains to analyze full-tweak-space counter cycling and determine whether it yields a stronger security bound.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{CTRT}$ instantiated with a tweakable block cipher whose tweak space $\mathcal{T}$ and block space $\mathcal{X}$ satisfy $|\mathcal{T}|>|\mathcal{X}|$, the existing $\mathrm{NSIV}$ composition analysis restricts the IV space to size at most $|\mathcal{X}|$. It can therefore be applied by choosing an IV subset $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathcal{T}$ of size $|\mathcal{X}|$ and letting the counter update $\operatorname{Inc}$ cycle over $\mathcal{I}$. Extend the security analysis to the variant in which $\operatorname{Inc}$ is a cyclic permutation of the entire tweak space $\mathcal{T}$, and determine whether this yields a stronger $\mathrm{CTRT}$ security bound.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption security analysis for CTRT over a tweakable block cipher with a larger tweak space than block space.
parameters: Tweak space 𝒯 and block space 𝒳: the tweak space has greater cardinality than the block space
IV subset ℐ: a subset of 𝒯 with the same cardinality as 𝒳 used by the existing analysis
Counter update Inc: cycles over ℐ in the existing application and over all of 𝒯 in the proposed variant
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the analysis to a cyclic counter update over the entire tweak space and determine whether the resulting CTRT security bound is stronger.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source gives a block-space-sized tweak subset that permits Theorem 1 to apply, then suggests that cycling over the entire tweak space may improve CTRT security without establishing the stronger bound.
citation_labels: Thomas Peyrin et al., Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers
